extracted.intended_audience: general readers and performers interested in the comedy roast genre (comedians, producers, and curious public)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and descriptive standards for producing or performing in a comedic roast — an insult-comedy event in which a guest of honor is mocked but also praised. Covers format, roles, consent, cultural/contextual constraints, and differences between live/televised/online roasting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — roast as insult comedy with praise and tributes
rubrics_metrics.description: A roast is a form of insult comedy ... in which a specific individual, a guest of honor, is subjected to jokes at their expense, as well as genuine praise and tributes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A proper roast explicitly mixes joking insults aimed at the honoree with sincere praise and tributes; the balance of these elements helps define the genre (not simply mean-spirited insults).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumption of good-humored reception / consent
rubrics_metrics.description: The assumption is that the roastee can take the jokes in good humor and not as serious criticism or insult.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roasts presuppose the target's willingness to be mocked; several passages emphasize that a 'true roast requires the consent of the target' and that solicitation/consent distinguishes roasts from plain harassment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content boundary — avoid being 'too insulting' given context
rubrics_metrics.description: In some cases, this has caused controversy when the host is seen as being too insulting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performers and hosts should calibrate insult intensity to context and audience; crossing perceived boundaries can produce backlash, controversy, or removal of material (examples cited include televised and live events criticized or taken down).

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of the roastmaster (host)
rubrics_metrics.description: The host of the event is called the roastmaster, since it rhymes with and plays on toastmaster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The roastmaster typically oversees the program, introduces roasters, manages pacing and transitions, and sets the tone (balancing insults and tributes). This role can shape acceptability and flow of the event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event structure / format — dais of roasters and turn-taking
rubrics_metrics.description: These events ... often featured a dais of comedians and celebrities who took turns roasting the honoree and each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Traditional roasts use a staged lineup of roasters who alternate short sets; televised adaptations often preserve this structure. Organizers should plan roaster order, time limits, and transitions to maintain tempo and variety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between solicited roasting and unsolicited insults (online risks)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is also a concept of roasting on internet social media, where a person asks others to mock them ... Though the mockery is solicited, this activity, too, has caused controversy, with some considering it a form of cyberbullying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Online 'RoastMe' style solicitations do not eliminate harm: performers/moderators and participants should be aware of cyberbullying risks and that consent in a public/viral online context may be ambiguous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private vs public setting affects permissible freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: The tradition has its roots in the raucous gatherings of the New York Friars Club ... These gatherings were private events where members could express themselves freely, often poking fun at each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content acceptable in a private, member-only roast may be inappropriate in public or broadcast settings; producers should adapt material to venue, membership, broadcast standards, and broader audience expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural and regional adaptation / sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedy Central's international affiliates began to produce and air their own local roasts ... Roasts have been adapted in the United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, India, China, Italy, etc., with varying formats and controversies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When adapting the roast format across countries or cultures, consider local sensibilities, censorship rules, and past controversies (e.g., events removed from platforms or criticized for offensive content). Localizing tone, targets, and limits is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Televised roast norms — maintain affectionate tribute with biting humor
rubrics_metrics.description: These events maintained the tradition's spirit, combining affectionate tribute with biting humor, and often featured a dais of comedians and celebrities who took turns roasting the honoree and each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Televised roasts aim to balance tribute and edge for entertainment value while navigating broadcast standards and public scrutiny; producers should select roasters, edit pacing, and anticipate reaction to particularly biting material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential for controversy and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: The programme [AIB Knockout] caused a controversy for allegedly featuring distasteful, sexist, offending, and humiliating content. Videos of the event were removed from YouTube.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizers and performers should recognize that controversial jokes can lead to platform removal, public backlash, or reputational harm; risk assessment and content moderation may be necessary.
